=====================================================================
HOW TO SWITCH ANALYTES (TP  <->  NOx)
=====================================================================
There are two config blocks, one per language (Quarto does not share
variables between R and Python here). To run the NOx analysis, edit:

  Python block : CHARACTERISTIC, VALUE_CAP, ANALYTE
  R block      : CHARACTERISTIC, VALUE_CAP, ANALYTE

The exact string to use for CHARACTERISTIC must match a value in the
'characteristic' column. To list the options, run once:

  pd.read_csv("data/cleaned_data_long.csv")["characteristic"].unique()
=====================================================================
-->

# Python EDA

```{python}
#| label: py-setup
import pandas as pd

# ── EDIT HERE to switch analyte ──────────────────────────────────
CHARACTERISTIC = "Phosphorus"   # exact string in the 'characteristic' column
VALUE_CAP      = 4              # drop obvious errors >= this; set None to keep all
ANALYTE        = "TP"           # short label used in printed output
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

SEASON = {12: "winter", 1: "winter", 2: "winter",
          3: "spring", 4: "spring", 5: "spring",
          6: "summer", 7: "summer", 8: "summer",
          9: "fall", 10: "fall", 11: "fall"}

# Load, parse the timestamp, and filter to the analyte of interest.
df = pd.read_csv("data/cleaned_data_long.csv", parse_dates=["date_time"])
df = df[df["characteristic"] == CHARACTERISTIC].copy()

# Optional single cap to drop obvious data-entry errors (applied once).
if VALUE_CAP is not None:
    n_dropped = int((df["measure_value"] >= VALUE_CAP).sum())
    df = df[df["measure_value"] < VALUE_CAP].copy()
    print(f"{ANALYTE}: dropped {n_dropped} rows >= cap {VALUE_CAP}")

df["season"] = df["month"].map(SEASON)

df.head()
```

Summary statistics

```{python}
#| label: py-describe
df["measure_value"].describe()
```

Count observations below the detection limit

```{python}
#| label: py-below-mdl
below = df["measure_value"] < df["mdl"]
print(f"{int(below.sum())} of {len(df)} observations below MDL")

# rows below MDL, for inspection
df.loc[below]
```

Observations per month / per season-site

```{python}
#| label: py-effort
# Very few winter observations is the recurring problem.
print(df.groupby("month").size())

# Sampling effort differs by season AND by season within site.
df.groupby(["season", "site"]).size()
```

Percent of calendar days sampled, by season

```{python}
#| label: py-coverage
# Unique sampling days (pooled across sites), labelled by season.
daily = (
    df.assign(date=df["date_time"].dt.normalize())
      .drop_duplicates("date")
)
daily["season"] = daily["date"].dt.month.map(SEASON)

# Every calendar day in the record window, labelled by season.
all_days = pd.date_range(df["date_time"].min().normalize(),
                         df["date_time"].max().normalize(), freq="D")
calendar = pd.DataFrame({"date": all_days})
calendar["season"] = calendar["date"].dt.month.map(SEASON)

coverage = pd.DataFrame({
    "observed_days": daily.groupby("season").size(),
    "possible_days": calendar.groupby("season").size(),
})
coverage["pct_present"] = 100 * coverage["observed_days"] / coverage["possible_days"]
coverage["pct_missing"] = 100 - coverage["pct_present"]
coverage
```


# R EDA & diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: r-setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)

# ── EDIT HERE to switch analyte ──────────────────────────────────
CHARACTERISTIC <- "Inorganic nitrogen (nitrate and nitrite)"   # exact string in the 'characteristic' column
VALUE_CAP      <- 15              # drop obvious errors >= this; set Inf to keep all
ANALYTE        <- "NOx (mg/L)"           # axis / title label
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

season_levels <- c("winter", "spring", "summer", "fall")

assign_season <- function(month) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    month %in% c(12, 1, 2)  ~ "winter",
    month %in% c(3, 4, 5)   ~ "spring",
    month %in% c(6, 7, 8)   ~ "summer",
    month %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "fall"
  )
}

# Load and clean ONCE. Everything downstream uses `dat`.
dat <- read.csv("data/cleaned_data_long.csv") %>%
  dplyr::filter(characteristic == CHARACTERISTIC, measure_value < VALUE_CAP) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    date_time = as.POSIXct(date_time),
    date      = lubridate::as_date(date_time),
    year      = lubridate::year(date_time),
    doy       = lubridate::yday(date_time),
    season    = factor(assign_season(month), levels = season_levels),
    below_mdl = dplyr::if_else(measure_value < mdl, 1, 0)
  )

# ── Reusable plot helpers ────────────────────────────────────────

# Create site labels
site_labs<- c("center_hill" = "Center Hill",
              "dale_hollow" = "Dale Hollow",
              "percy_priest" = "Percy Priest")

# Scatter of measure_value vs a chosen x, smoothed, faceted by site.
plot_scatter <- function(data, xvar, xlab = NULL,
                         smooth_method = "gam", smooth_formula = y ~ s(x)) {
  ggplot(data, aes({{ xvar }}, measure_value)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_smooth(method = smooth_method, formula = smooth_formula) +
    facet_wrap(~ site, scales = "free_y",
                labeller = as_labeller(site_labs)) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ANALYTE) +
    theme_bw()
}

# Density of measure_value, optionally on the log scale.
plot_density <- function(data, log = FALSE) {
  d <- dplyr::mutate(data, .x = if (log) log(measure_value) else measure_value)
  ggplot(d, aes(.x)) +
    geom_density(fill = "grey85", color = "grey30") +
    labs(x = if (log) paste0("log(", ANALYTE, ")") else ANALYTE) +
    theme_bw()
}
```

Core relationships: over time, by distance, and distribution shape

```{r}
#| label: r-core
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Over time, per site.
plot_scatter(dat, date_time, xlab = NULL)+
  theme(text = element_text(size = 13))

# By total distance, per site (looser default smoother).
plot_scatter(dat, total_distance, xlab = "Total distance from dam",
             smooth_method = "loess", smooth_formula = y ~ x)+
            theme(text = element_text(size = 13))

# Distribution: raw is right-skewed (gamma-like)...
plot_density(dat, log = FALSE)

# ...log-transformed is closer to normal (residuals are what matter).
plot_density(dat, log = TRUE)
```

Collection effort by season

```{r}
#| label: r-effort
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# measure_value vs month: far more data in summer than winter.
ggplot(dat, aes(month, measure_value)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(y = ANALYTE) +
  theme_bw()

# n by season within site: winter is unusable, spring is a stretch.
dat %>%
  dplyr::count(season, site) %>%
  ggplot(aes(season, n)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~ site) +
  theme_bw()

# Timeline colored by season, per site.
ggplot(dat, aes(date_time, measure_value, color = season)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ site) +
  theme_bw()

# Day-of-year by year, to see the within-year sampling window.
ggplot(dat, aes(doy, measure_value)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(year))
```


# Deep dive: seasonal trends in missingness

```{r}
#| label: r-coverage
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# =====================================================================
# (1) Year x season x reservoir coverage
# Is the SEASONAL COMPOSITION of sampling stable across years?
# Pooled counts hide drift. Drift here aliases into any s(date) trend.
# =====================================================================
coverage <- dat %>%
  dplyr::count(site, year, season, name = "n") %>%
  tidyr::complete(site, year, season, fill = list(n = 0))

# Raw counts as a labelled tile grid.
p1_counts <- ggplot(coverage, aes(year, season, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey90") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), size = 2.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ site, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1) +
  labs(title = "Sample count by year x season", x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "n") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

# Composition within each year -- the drift check.
# Look for: bars whose seasonal mix shifts left to right. A stable trend
# model needs seasonal proportions roughly constant, or season carried
# explicitly so the trend is conditional.
p1_comp <- coverage %>%
  group_by(site, year) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, prop, fill = season)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ site, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "mako", end = 0.9) +
  labs(title = "Seasonal composition of sampling, within year",
       x = NULL, y = "proportion of samples", fill = "season") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

print(p1_counts)
print(p1_comp)
```

```{r}
#| label: r-censoring
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# =====================================================================
# (2) Censoring rate by season x reservoir, plus MDL over time
# Confirm whether the unsampled season is also the least-censored
# regime, and rule out a drifting detection limit masquerading as trend.
# =====================================================================
cens_summary <- dat %>%
  group_by(site, season) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    n_cens   = sum(below_mdl, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_cens = round(100 * n_cens / n, 1),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(site, season)

print(cens_summary, n = Inf)

# Censoring by year, to separate environmental from lab drift.
cens_by_year <- dat %>%
  group_by(site, year) %>%
  summarise(pct_cens = round(100 * mean(below_mdl, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop")

p2_cens <- ggplot(cens_by_year, aes(year, pct_cens, color = site)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Percent below MDL by year", x = NULL, y = "% censored") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

# Distinct detection limits and the windows they apply to.
# Look for: MDL steps that line up with changes in pct_cens.
mdl_windows <- dat %>%
  group_by(mdl, date) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(mdl, date)

print(mdl_windows)

p2_mdl <- ggplot(dat, aes(date, mdl, color = site)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Detection limit over time", x = NULL, y = "MDL") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

print(p2_cens)
print(p2_mdl)
```

```{r}
#| label: r-seasonal-dist
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# =====================================================================
# (3) Raw values by season x reservoir, censored points flagged
# How strongly seasonal is the response? Sets the stakes of the missing
# winter. Censored values are drawn at their limit and flagged.
# Look for: heavy overlap across seasons => low-stakes winter gap;
# strong separation => the gap is an inference problem.
# =====================================================================
p3 <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    below_mdl_bool = below_mdl == 1,
    plot_val       = if_else(measure_value < mdl, mdl, measure_value)  # censored sit at limit
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(season, plot_val)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "grey92", color = "grey70", scale = "width") +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = below_mdl_bool, shape = below_mdl_bool),
              width = 0.18, height = 0, alpha = 0.6, size = 1.3) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey30", `TRUE` = "firebrick"),
                     labels = c("observed", "<= MDL")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 2),
                     labels = c("observed", "<= MDL")) +
  facet_wrap(~ site) +
  labs(title = paste0(ANALYTE, " by season (censored values shown at the detection limit)"),
       x = NULL, y = paste0(ANALYTE, " (log scale)"), color = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

print(p3)
```

```{r}
#| label: r-intervals
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# =====================================================================
# (4) Sampling-interval distribution per reservoir
# Make the winter gaps explicit and gauge how much the CAR1 / GP term
# can learn. Gaps are computed WITHIN a station series (id), not pooled
# across stations (pooling invents spurious tiny gaps).
# =====================================================================
intervals <- dat %>%
  arrange(site, id, date) %>%
  group_by(site, id) %>%
  mutate(gap_days = as.numeric(date - lag(date))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(gap_days), gap_days > 0)

interval_summary <- intervals %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  summarise(
    median_gap = median(gap_days),
    q90_gap    = quantile(gap_days, 0.90),
    max_gap    = max(gap_days),
    n_gaps     = n(),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

print(interval_summary)

# Look for: a long right tail / large max_gap is the winter hole.
p4 <- ggplot(intervals, aes(gap_days)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~ site, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Days between consecutive samples (within station)",
       x = "gap (days)", y = "count") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

print(p4)
```

```{r}
#| label: r-span
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# =====================================================================
# (5) Record span and n per reservoir
# Are the three reservoirs comparable in record length and replication
# before any trend contrast is attempted?
# =====================================================================
span <- dat %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  summarise(
    n          = n(),
    first      = min(date),
    last       = max(date),
    span_yrs   = round(as.numeric(difftime(max(date), min(date),
                                           units = "days")) / 365.25, 1),
    n_years    = n_distinct(year),
    n_stations = n_distinct(id),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

print(span)

# Timeline strip: every sample as a point, colored by season.
# Look for: differing record windows, and visible winter voids.
p5 <- ggplot(dat, aes(date, site, color = season)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(height = 0.15), alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "mako", end = 0.9) +
  labs(title = "Sample timing by reservoir", x = NULL, y = NULL, color = "season") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

print(p5)
```


## MDL over time, with observed values

```{r}
#| label: r-mdl-trend
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# One row per site-date so the MDL step pattern is not over-plotted.
dat %>%
  distinct(site, date, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  ggplot(aes(date, mdl)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "cadetblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ site) +
  theme_bw()
# monotonic decline in MDL over time, which makes sense
```
